question: What will Statistics Poland's flash estimate of Poland's Q3 2026 GDP growth be?

calls.reasoning: Late-Oct bank nowcasts for Q3 2026 y/y: PKO BP ~3.3 (Oct 29; earlier ~3.0), ING ~3.5 (Sep), Credit Agricole 3.7 (Oct 22), mBank 3.6-3.8, Pekao 3.8-3.9; median ~3.6-3.7. Weak September construction (-9% y/y) and slower retail argue down; strong September industry (+4.6%) and an extra working day vs Q3 2025 (66 vs 65 by my count) argue up. Q2 was revised to 4.1. Flash surprises vs consensus are typically 0.3-0.4pp. No prediction market found (Polymarket/Kalshi list only US/eurozone GDP).
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off GUS flash ('szybki szacunek') Q3 2026 GDP y/y, NSA, constant prices; due 13 Nov 2026. Later revisions do not count.
- Event window: single release on 13 Nov 2026; as of 2026-11-03 it is not yet published.
- Q2 2026 revised to 4.1% y/y and Q1 to 3.7% (GUS revision of 16 Oct 2026, about +0.2pp).
- PKO BP (PAP, 29 Oct 2026): Q3 about 3.3% y/y; an earlier 20 Oct note said about 3%. Cites weak September construction (-9% y/y), durables production -7.3%, and a cycle peak at the turn of 2025-26.
- ING BSK (wnp.pl, 22 Sep 2026): Q3 about 3.5%; investment possibly above 8.4% y/y; consumption above 3%. This predates the GUS revision.
- Credit Agricole (wnp.pl, 22 Oct 2026): Q3 3.7%; consumption 3.1% vs 2.8% in Q2. An earlier CA projection was 3.3%, made before the revision.
- mBank (analizy.pl, 30 Oct 2026): full-year 2026 raised to 3.9%; weak construction may reduce Q3, with part recovered in Q4. Question background puts mBank's Q3 at 3.6-3.8.
- Pekao: Q3 3.8-3.9% y/y per search snippets and question background.
- September industrial production +4.6% y/y (consensus 3.1%); retail sales +3.3%; construction about -9% vs +2.4% expected.
- Working days: Q3 2026 has 66 vs 65 in Q3 2025 (own count; Aug 15 falls on a Saturday in 2026 vs a Friday in 2025), which is positive for the NSA y/y figure.
- No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold market for Poland Q3 GDP was found.
- Searched for but not found: a PAP/Parkiet consensus survey median for Q3 flash.
calls.reference_class: Polish GDP flash estimates vs late bank nowcast consensus (flash typically within +/-0.5pp of consensus median)

calls.reasoning: Q2 2026 was revised to 4.1% y/y; Q3 monthly data are mixed: industry is strong (Aug 4.0%, Sep 4.6%), construction is weak (Jul -2.4%, Sep -9%) and retail sales slowed to 3.3%. Bank estimates range from PKO BP ~3% (20 Oct) and ING ~3.5% (22 Sep; later H2 ~3%) to mBank 3.6-3.9% and Pekao 3.8-3.9%. By my calendar count Q3 2026 had one more working day than Q3 2025 (66 vs 65), which helps the unadjusted y/y rate. Median 3.6, spread at the usual flash-vs-consensus error. No prediction market found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold.

- Event window: Q3 2026 data (Jul-Sep) is complete; the only remaining event is the publication on 13 Nov. As of 2026-11-03 the outcome is fixed but not yet published.
- GUS revision of 16 Oct 2026: Q1 2026 3.7% y/y, Q2 2026 4.1% y/y (about +0.2pp revisions) (question background).

- ING BSK (wnp.pl, 22 Sep 2026): Q3 GDP ~3.5% y/y; consumption expected back above 3% (Q2 2.8%), investment possibly above Q2's 8.4%. A later ING outlook put H2 2026 growth at ~3% y/y and full-year 2026 at 3.4% (search snippet).
- mBank (analizy.pl, Oct 2026): Q3 possibly ~3.9% (earlier 3.7%); weaker construction may cut Q3, partly recovered in Q4. Question background: mBank ~3.6-3.8, Pekao ~3.8-3.9.
- Monthly data: industrial production Aug +4.0%, Sep +4.6% y/y (consensus 3.1); construction Jul -2.4%, Sep about -9% y/y (consensus +2.4); retail sales Sep +3.3% (Aug 3.8%).
- Calendar: by my count Q3 2026 had 66 working days vs 65 in Q3 2025 (Aug 15, 2026 falls on a Saturday), a small boost to the NSA y/y rate.
- Base rates: GUS flash vs late consensus typical absolute miss ~0.2-0.4pp (my approximation, not sourced this run); the full range of bank estimates this quarter is about 3.0-3.9.
- Not found: a formal PAP/Bloomberg consensus for the flash; any prediction market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold; any GUS hint.

- PKO BP (wnp.pl, 2026-10-20): Q3 GDP growth slowed to ~3% y/y from 4.1% in Q2; industry broad-based (supply goods +8.9%), construction -9% y/y called a surprise similar to July; growth reliant on public/defence demand.
- PKO BP's Marta Petka-Zagajewska (strefainwestorow.pl, 2026-10-29): 'preliminarily estimate Q3 GDP grew 3.3% y/y'; says the cycle peak has passed.
- ING BSK (wnp.pl, 2026-09-22): Q3 ~3.5% y/y, assumed consumption >3% and investment above Q2's 8.4%; made before the weak September construction data.

- Credit Agricole (search snippet): Q3 3.3% y/y.

- Monthly Q3 data: industry Sept +4.6% (Aug +4.0%); construction Sept -9% (seasonally adjusted -7.2%); retail Sept +3.3%.
- Status quo/anchor: the spread of bank nowcasts runs 3.0-3.9; historically GUS flash prints differ from consensus by about 0.3-0.4pp.
- Resolution: resolves off the GUS flash ('szybki szacunek') non-seasonally-adjusted y/y figure for Q3 2026, due around 13 Nov 2026; not the later 'wstępny' estimate.

calls.reference_class: Polish GUS flash GDP y/y prints relative to the median of bank nowcasts published 2-4 weeks before release

calls.reasoning: Current bank nowcasts for Q3 2026 y/y NSA: PKO 3.3 (Oct 29), Credit Agricole 3.7 (Oct 22, post-revision), mBank 3.6-3.8, Pekao 3.8-3.9; ING's 3.5 is stale (Sep). Median ~3.7. Weak September construction (-9%) and slower retail argue a bit lower; strong industry and one extra working day vs Q3 2025 (66 vs 65, verified) argue higher. Q2 revised to 4.1, so slowdown is consensus. Center 3.65, spread at typical flash-vs-consensus error. No prediction market found (runs checked Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold).
calls.reconciliation: Disputed facts: PKO's estimate (3.0 on Oct 20 superseded by 3.3 on Oct 29, which is used); Credit Agricole 3.3 vs 3.7 (3.3 predates the 16 Oct GUS upward revision, so 3.7 is current); mBank 3.6-3.8 vs ~3.9 (the 3.9 may be its full-year figure; unresolved without web access, so treated as ~3.7). Working days checked by own calendar computation: Q3 2026 has 66 vs 65 in Q3 2025, a small upside to the NSA figure that banks likely already partly include. Judgment: centre slightly below the ~3.7 current-estimate median because of the September construction collapse, and partly offset by the calendar effect; 3.65. Width carried forward from Runs 1-2 (~1.1), slightly narrowed. No new sources retrieved this run.
